questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. Both Rajesh as well as his wife (1)/ are determined to bring (2)/ about some changes in the plan. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. 

Both Rajesh as well as his wife (1)/ are determined to bring (2)/ about some changes in the plan. (3)/ No Error (4)

options.text: Both Rajesh as well as his wife
options.html: Both Rajesh as well as his wife

options.text: about some changes in the plan.
options.html: about some changes in the plan.

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is '1'.
 Key Points
  • In the given sentence, the error is in the usage of words "as well as", we have to use "and" in its place
  • Here, the words "both" and "and" are used together when we connect subjects or objects.

Hence, the correct sentence will be: Both Rajesh and his wife are determined to bring about some changes in the plan.

  

  • दिए गए वाक्य में, त्रुटि(Error) शब्द "as well as" के उपयोग में है, हमें इसके स्थान पर "and" का उपयोग करना होगा |
  • यहां, "both" और "and" शब्दों का उपयोग एक साथ किया जाता है जब हम विषय या वस्तु जुड़ते हैं।

इसलिए, सही वाक्य होगा:-  Both Rajesh and his wife are determined to bring about some changes in the plan.

questions.solution: We often use question tags when we expect the listener to agree with our statement. In this case, when the statement is positive, we use a negative question tag. questions.question: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error. My cousin is not like going for a walk very much.

The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.

My cousin is not like going for a walk very much.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is "is not like"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the verb "is" is incorrect.
  • The verb "is" is a stative verb.
  • Stative verbs represent a state of being or a condition.
    • Example: He is unconscious due to the sedatives from the operation.
  • In the given sentence, we need to use an action verb since the sentence is describing an action.
  • Action verbs are those verbs that describe what a person, animal, thing, or process can do.
  • The appropriate action verb form will be 'does'.
  • In the given sentence, 'does' describes what the subject of the sentence is not fond of doing.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
     

The correct sentence is: My cousin does not like going for a walk very much.

questions.question: Direction: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I could have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I could have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is could have​.

Key Points

  • ​Conditional sentences are statements discussing known factors or hypothetical situations and their consequences.
  • One of the structures is mentioned below:
  • This particular type is followed when something didn't happen as a certain condition wasn't fulfilled.
    • If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.
    • Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (alternative structure)
  • Example:
    • If I had noticed you, I would had call you.
    • If I had noticed you, I would have called you.
    • Had I noticed you, I would have called you.
  • To follow the given structure correctly, 'would have' will replace 'could have' in the part given in the 3rd option.
     

Correct Sentence: Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I would have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.

 ​​​​Additional Information

  • There is one more type of conditional sentence in the past tense given below:
  • This particular type is followed when we talk about something in the past which is purely imaginary.
    • If + Simple Past, Subject + Would + V1 + Object.
  • Example:
    • If I had wings, I would fly like a bird.

Hinglish

  • सशर्त वाक्य (conditional sentence) ज्ञात कारकों या काल्पनिक स्थितियों और उनके परिणामों पर चर्चा करने वाले बयान हैं।
  • संरचनाओं में से एक का उल्लेख नीचे किया गया है:
  • इस विशेष प्रकार का पालन तब किया जाता है जब कुछ नहीं हुआ क्योंकि एक निश्चित शर्त पूरी नहीं हुई थी।
    • If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.
    • Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (वैकल्पिक संरचना)
  • उदाहरण:
    • If I had noticed you, I would had call you.
    • If I had noticed you, I would have called you.
    • Had I noticed you, I would have called you.
  • दी गई संरचना का सही ढंग से पालन करने के लिए, तीसरे विकल्प में दिए गए भाग में 'could have' के स्थान पर 'would have' होगा।
    ​

सही वाक्य: Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I would have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.

Additional Information 

  • नीचे दिए गए भूत काल में एक और प्रकार का सशर्त वाक्य (conditional sentence) है:
  • इस विशेष प्रकार का अनुसरण तब किया जाता है जब हम अतीत में किसी ऐसी चीज के बारे में बात करते हैं जो विशुद्ध रूप से काल्पनिक है।
    • If + Simple Past, Subject + Would + V1 + Object.
  • उदाहरण:
    • If I had wings, I would fly like a bird.

questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Many pilgrims died in a stampede while boarding (1)/ a private ferry to the holy place on (2)/ the ﬁrst day of the ten day long festival. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  •  The entire sentence is grammatically correct.
  • Part (1): “while boarding a private ferry”
    • “While boarding” is a correct present participial phrase showing the time/ongoing action.
    • It correctly modifies “Many pilgrims”, the subject of the sentence.
    • The verb–object structure boarding a private ferry is grammatically sound.
  • Part (2): “on the first day of the ten day long festival”
    • The preposition “on” is correctly used with specific days.
    • “First day” is a countable, definite time reference, so “the” is appropriate.
    • “Ten day long” functions as a compound adjective describing “festival” and is acceptable in exam usage.
  • Overall sentence correctness:
    • Subject–verb agreement is correct (pilgrims died).
    • Tense is consistent (simple past for a completed event).
    • All modifiers are logically and grammatically placed.

Hence, the entire sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After a long gap, / we went shopping / last Sunday and bought / that we wanted.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After a long gap, / we went shopping / last Sunday and bought / that we wanted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'that we wanted' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the conjunction 'that' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is talking about some people purchasing whatever they wanted.
  • The conjunction 'that' is used for introducing a subordinate clause expressing a statement or hypothesis.
  • The pronoun 'what' should be used in place of the conjunction 'that'.
  • The pronoun 'what' means whatever (referring to the whole of an amount).
  • Therefore, the pronoun 'what' should be used in place of the conjunction 'that'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: After a long gap, we went shopping last Sunday and bought what we wanted.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में conjunction 'that' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य कुछ लोगों के बारे में बात कर रहा है कि वे जो कुछ भी चाहते थे उसे खरीद रहे थे।
  • एक कथन या परिकल्पना को व्यक्त करने वाले subordinate clause को पेश करने के लिए conjunction 'that' का उपयोग किया जाता है।
  • Conjunction 'that' के स्थान पर pronoun 'what' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • Pronoun 'what' का अर्थ है जो कुछ भी।
  • इसलिए, conjunction 'that' के स्थान पर pronoun 'what' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

सही वाक्य: After a long gap, we went shopping last Sunday and bought what we wanted.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. There is a man sitting beside cat. .

Key Points

  • The given sentence has a grammatical error concerning the use of prepositions.
  • The word "beside" should be followed by an article "a" or "the" before the noun "cat".
  • The correct sentence should be "There is a man sitting beside a/the cat".

Correct sentence: There is a man sitting beside a/the cat.

Additional Information

  • Use of Prepositions:
    • Beside: This preposition means "next to" or "at the side of". It often needs to be followed by an article when referring to a specific noun.
    • Example: She sits beside the fireplace.
  • Other Common Prepositions:
    • In: Used to indicate location or position within something.
    • On: Used to indicate surface or position on a surface.
    • At: Used to indicate a specific point or place.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: poured the contents

Key Points

  • The error lies in the verb tense.
  • The verb "say" is in the present tense, indicating that the instructions are providing current guidance.
  • The verb "poured" should be changed to "pour" to maintain proper verb tense agreement.
  • The correct sentence should maintain consistency in verb tense. 
  • Corrected sentence: "The instructions on the bottle say – open the packet and pour the contents into hot water."
  • Both "open" and "pour" are in the present tense, ensuring agreement with the initial verb "say."

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • Verb tense agreement refers to the consistent use of verb forms in a sentence or a paragraph.
  • It ensures that the timing of the actions described in the sentence is clear and logical.
  • There are three primary verb tenses: past, present, and future, each with its own forms.
